# ng-magic-test-bed (Jasmine)

> A magic test bed for angular

> Generated by compodoc 2.0.0 at 2026-10-30T21:01:13.048Z, llm-md export.

### NgMagicSetupTestBed

File: `src/setup-test-bed/ng-magic-setup-test-bed.class.ts`
Extends: `NgMagicTestBed`

Methods:
- `componentMocks(componentClass: Type<C>): MockArray<C>` — declare that you want to generically mock all inputs and outputs of a component and retrieve all created component mock instances after fixture creation. auto-generated mock class that was queried for, usable with fixture.debugElement.query(By.directive(...)) at any point in your test, since you no longer have a reference to this class yourself) and requery() (re-runs the same query against the fixture's current DOM and rewrites this array in place - does not call detectChanges() itself). The array's members can only be used after calling .fixture(). Before that time the array is initialized like this: \['this array can only be used after fixture() was called'\].
- `componentProviderMock(componentClass: Type<any>, token: ProviderToken<S>, mock?: M, dontSpy: unknown = false, spySource?: AbstractType<Partial<S>>): unknown | unknown` — If you have component provides a provider you can mock it using this method.
- `componentServiceMock(componentClass: Type<any>, serviceClass: AbstractType<S>, mock: M, dontSpy: unknown): S & M`

- `declarations(declarations: Array<any>): void` — check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `directiveMocks(directiveClass: Type<C>): MockArray<C>` — declare that you want to mock a directive for a selector and retrieve all created component mock instances after fixture creation. Note that this method behaves different to directiveMocks. This is because Angular is missing a public reflectDirectiveType method. This method will be made smarter as soon as such a method is available. class that was queried for, usable with fixture.debugElement.query(By.directive(...)) at any point in your test) and requery() (re-runs the same query against the fixture's current DOM and rewrites this array in place - does not call detectChanges() itself). The array's members can only be used after calling .fixture(). Before that time the array is initialized like this: \['this array can only be used after fixture() was called'\].
- `directiveProviderMock(directiveClass: Type<any>, token: ProviderToken<S>, mock?: M, dontSpy: unknown = false, spySource?: AbstractType<any>): unknown | unknown` — If you have directive that provides a provider you can mock it using this method.
- `directiveServiceMock(directiveClass: Type<any>, serviceClass: AbstractType<S>, mock: M, dontSpy: unknown): S & M` — If you have directive that provides a service you can mock it using this method.
- `factoryMock(factoryClass: AbstractType<F>, instances: Array<M & I>): SpyObj<F>` — mocks a service that has a "create" method. The first call of mock.create() will return the first item in the instances-array and so on.
- `fixture(componentClass: Type<C>, initialInputs: MagicFixtureInputs<C> = {}, disableNoErrorSchema: unknown = false): ComponentFixture<C>` — Use this method to create a component fixture. This method may only be called once per NgMagicTestBed instance. ComponentRef.setInput() - works for both classic @Input()-decorated properties and signal-based input() properties. For a signal input created with a transform , provide the transform's input type (the same type you'd write in a template binding) - it will be transformed the same way Angular does for real bindings. throwing exceptions e.g. for missing or unknown inputs.
- `import(aImport: any): void` — check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `imports(imports: any[]): void` — check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `injection(token: ProviderToken<S>): S` — return you the service or provider for a given token from the angular dependency injection. This will trigger the TestBed configureTestingModule step. After this step you can not create any more mocks. Make sure you create all your mocks before calling this method.
- `interfaceMock(mock: Partial<I>, dontSpy: unknown = false): I & SpyObj` — Creates a mock object that satisfies the shape of a TypeScript interface I. This does not (and cannot) replace I anywhere - interfaces have no runtime representation, so there is no prototype to reflect on the way objectMock() reflects on a class. Only the methods you actually provide in mock become spies - nothing can be auto-generated for members you omit, since there is nothing to reflect on for those either. mock only has to be a Partial , so omitted members are typed as present (I & SpyObj ) but do not actually exist on the returned object - calling one you didn't provide throws at runtime despite compiling. Use this instead of objectMock(undefined, mock) purely to avoid casting the result to I & SpyObj yourself. implementation you supplied, like objectMock() does.
- `keptComponentImports(keptComponentImports: Array<Type<any>>): void` — Declare that you want to keep several pipes/directives/standalone components exactly as they are, in one call. Each one is added to the imports (or declarations, for non-standalone classes) of your fixture component and all other kept components - the same effect as calling keptPipe() once per item, but without the per-item boilerplate and without querying for instances afterward. Typical use: keeping Angular's own structural directives/pipes (NgIf, NgFor, AsyncPipe, ...) that your fixture component's template relies on, since overriding a standalone component's imports for fixture/mock purposes replaces its imports array entirely - see keptDirectives()/keptComponents() if you also need access to the rendered instances afterward.
- `keptComponents(componentClass: Type<C>): MockArray<C>` — Declare that you want to keep a certain component. This kept component will be added to the imports of your fixture component and all other kept components. class that was queried for, usable with fixture.debugElement.query(By.directive(...)) at any point in your test) and requery() (re-runs the same query against the fixture's current DOM and rewrites this array in place - does not call detectChanges() itself). The array's members can only be used after calling .fixture(). Before that time the array is initialized like this: \['this array can only be used after fixture() was called'\].
- `keptDirectives(directiveClass: Type<C>): MockArray<C>` — Declare that you want to keep a certain directive. This kept directive will be added to the imports of your fixture component and all kept components.
- `keptPipe(pipeClass: Type<C>): void` — declare that you want to keep a pipe for a selector.
- `objectMock(objectClass: AbstractType<O>, mock: M, dontSpy: unknown): O & M` — Can be used to create a mock for an object that should not be registered at angular TestBed. In addition to that a spy will be added for each additional method that was found on the objectClass' prototype.
- `observer(observable: Observable<T>, name?: string): SpyObserver<T>` — Subscribes to a given observable and spies on its states and emitted values. Observable you want to spy Optional name that prefixes all spies that are created by the observer. This makes it easier to read the test output if anything fails. observer that can be used to make assertions in your test cases e.g.: expect(observer.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue); For more information check SpyObserver documentation
- `outputObserver(output: OutputEmitterRef<T>, name?: string): SpyObserver<T>` — Subscribes to a given output and spies on its states and emitted values. Output you want to spy Optional name that prefixes all spies that are created by the observer. This makes it easier to read the test output if anything fails. outputObserver that can be used to make assertions in your test cases e.g.: expect(outputObserver.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue); For more information check SpyObserver documentation
- `pipeMock(pipeName: string, transform?: function): Spy` — declare that you want to mock a pipe for a selector.
- `provider(provider: any): void` — check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `providerFunctionMock(token: InjectionToken<F>, callback?: Partial<F> & Func): Spy<F>` — replaces a function that is provided with an angular provider token with a spy
- `providerMock(token: ProviderToken<S>, mock: M, dontSpy: boolean = false, spySource?: AbstractType<Partial<S>>): unknown | unknown` — mocks a provider for a given token with a given mock. If wanted your mock can be extended by spies from a given spySource class. In addition to that a spy will be added for each additional method that was found on the objectClass' prototype.
- `providers(providers: any[]): void` — check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `run(): void` — Can be used to run a callback in injection context. Like TestBed.runInInjectionContext(). Additionally this will trigger the TestBed configureTestingModule step. After this step you can not create any more mocks. Make sure you create all your mocks before calling this method. This method can be used to configure the testing module when used without
- `schema(schema: SchemaMetadata | any[]): void` — is pushed by default. This can be disabled when calling .fixture(). check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `schemas(schemas: Array<SchemaMetadata | []>): void` — is pushed by default. This can be disabled when calling .fixture(). check out angular docs for more information https://angular.io/guide/testing-services#angular-testbed https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestBed#configuretestingmodule https://angular.io/api/core/testing/TestModuleMetadata
- `serviceMock(serviceClass: AbstractType<S>, mock: M, dontSpy: unknown): S & M`

### SpyObserver

File: `src/observe/spy-observer.class.ts`

Description: Subscribes to a given observable and tracks all observations.

Properties:
- `complete: Spy` — your test framework's spy that will be called when the observable completes Can be uses like this: expect(observer.complete).toHaveBeenCalled();
- `error: Spy` — your test framework's spy that will be called when the observable throws an error Can be uses like this: expect(observer.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedError);
- `next: Spy` — your test framework's spy that will be called when the observable emits a value. Can be uses like this: expect(observer.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue);
- `observations: Array<T> = []` — When the observable emits a value, it will be pushed onto this array.

## Public functions

- `mock(spySource?: AbstractType, mock: M = <any>{}, dontSpy?: boolean): unknown | unknown` — Can be used to create a mock for an object that is an instance of a class.
  Defined in `src/mock/mock.function.ts`
- `mockComponent(ComponentClass: Type): Type<MockedComponent<T>>`
  Defined in `src/mock/mock-component.function.ts`
- `mockInterface(mock: Partial, dontSpy: unknown = false): I & SpyObj` — Creates a mock object that satisfies the shape of a TypeScript interface I, without needing an NgMagicTestBed instance. Standalone alternative to magic.interfaceMock(). This does not (and cannot) replace I anywhere - interfaces have no runtime representation, so there is no prototype to reflect on the way mock() reflects on a class. Only the methods you actually provide in mock become spies - nothing can be auto-generated for members you omit, since there is nothing to reflect on for those either. mock only has to be a Partial , so omitted members are typed as present (I & SpyObj ) but do not actually exist on the returned object - calling one you didn't provide throws at runtime despite compiling.
  Defined in `src/mock/mock-interface.function.ts`
- `observe(observable: Observable, name?: string)`
  Defined in `src/observe/observe.function.ts`
- `spyOnFunctionsOf(target: any, source?: any)`
  Defined in `src/spy-on-functions/spy-on-functions-of.function.ts`

## Public type aliases

- `type MagicFixtureInputs = Partial<UnwrapInputSignal<C['K']>>`
- `type MockArray = Array<C> & literal type` — An array of component or directive instances found inside the fixture, extended with two extras: mockClass: the class that was used to query the fixture's DOM for these instances. Use it directly with fixture.debugElement.query(By.directive(...)) whenever you need the DebugElement/nativeElement, at any point in your test - not just right after fixture() was called. requery(): re-runs the same query against the fixture's current DOM and rewrites this array in place with whatever it finds now. Does NOT call detectChanges() itself - call that first if you need it.
- `type MockedComponent = T & unknown`
- `type UnwrapInputSignal = unknown`
